html:
The global order is being significantly reshaped by the escalating conflict in the Middle East, with the "Iran war" dominating discussions at the BRICS summit and tensions rising around crucial maritime chokepoints. New attacks on an Iranian cargo ship and a Saudi oil pipeline underscore the immediate security and economic risks.

Middle East Conflicts: Fighting in Yemen has intensified, with Iran-backed Houthi forces capturing strategic territory around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and reportedly controlling both the Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz Strait, posing an "unprecedented threat" to global shipping. Saudi Arabia was forced to shut down a crucial Red Sea pipeline after it came under attack, with US president Donald Trump stating that Iran is probably responsible and Saudi Arabia condemning a drone attack from Iraq. An Iranian commercial vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one person, as Iran prepares for talks with Iraq and Gulf nations in Oman regarding new maritime arrangements in the Strait. Bahrain will not attend this Iran-GCC summit. In Gaza, medics report Israeli strikes killed two people, including parents and two children, while a film documenting the systematic killing in Gaza received a record standing ovation at the Venice Film Festival.

Geopolitical Blocs: The 18th BRICS summit, hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, brought together leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. While members agreed on the need for a new global order, divisions were exposed, as the summit did not condemn the "US-Israel war on Iran." Modi warned that geopolitical tensions and supply chain shocks threaten global stability. Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin warned that sending European troops to Ukraine would mean war with Russia, as a Russian drone hit a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train near the Polish border. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, in an interview, offered to meet Putin at the G20 in Miami.

The Future of AI: Concerns over the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence are growing, with ex-Anthropic researchers expressing genuine fear for humanity's future and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calling for development to be slowed down due to "serious" risks. Ex-president Barack Obama reportedly urged Democrats to prioritize a sweeping framework for AI safety, while US president Donald Trump dismissed some of these concerns as exaggerated, and some in Silicon Valley met stark warnings with skepticism.

European Political Shifts: Sweden is heading into a close general election, with the far right eyeing a role in government as it gains ground by addressing concerns over crime and security. In France, Marine Le Pen has launched her presidential campaign, despite wearing an electronic tag following a recent conviction, while staff at public broadcaster Radio France went on strike over the appointment of Charles Sapin, deputy editor-in-chief at far-right weekly Valeurs Actuelles.

Global Economic & Social Issues: Reform UK has received substantial donations of £72m from billionaires, sparking debate over its political prospects and the legality of the funds, with Labour’s Angela Rayner warning of possible retrospective action. Separately, Turkish police have detained dozens in raids on gay bars and homes of LGBTQ+ activists, with human rights groups accusing the government of targeting the LGBTQ+ community. In Indonesia, a ferry capsized in the Java Sea amid bad weather, leaving six dead and approximately 130 people missing in the second major ferry accident in five days.
